front.title: Deterministic Networking (DetNet) Data Plane - guaranteed Latency Based Forwarding (gLBF) for bounded latency with low jitter and asynchronous forwarding in Deterministic Networks

abstract.t:
This memo proposes a mechanism called "guaranteed Latency Based Forwarding" (gLBF) as part of DetNet for hop-by-hop packet forwarding with per-hop deterministically bounded latency and minimal jitter.
gLBF is intended to be useful across a wide range of networks and applications that need high-precision deterministic networking services, from in-car networks and networks for industrial automation on factory floors all the way to country-wide networks at 100 Gbps and beyond.
Unlike other mechanisms, gLBF does not require network-wide clock synchronization, nor does it require per-flow state on network nodes. It thereby avoids the drawbacks of other known methods while retaining their advantages.
Specifically, gLBF uses the queuing model and calculus of Urgency Based Scheduling (UBS, [UBS]), which is used by TSN Asynchronous Traffic Shaping [TSN-ATS]. gLBF is intended as a plug-in replacement for, or a mechanism in parallel to, TSN-ATS, because it allows reuse of the same controller-plane design that selects paths for TSN-ATS, sizes TSN-ATS queues, calculates latencies and admits flows onto the calculated paths with the calculated latencies.
In addition to reducing jitter compared to TSN-ATS through additional buffering (dampening) in the network, gLBF also eliminates the per- flow, per-hop state maintenance required by TSN-ATS. This avoids having to signal per-flow state from the controller-plane to every hop, and the associated scaling problems. It also reduces the implementation cost of high-speed networking hardware, because it avoids the additional high-speed read/write memory accesses needed to retrieve, process and update per-flow state variables for a large number of flows.
